messages.author: 2c54c398ac8b7657
messages.subject: R ctmm errors
parts:
Hi,

I am new to ctmm and still beginner in r.
I try to derive homeranges from animal tracking data using the aKDE (ctmm) approach.
I applied the same workflow as used in the provided example in the ctmm.pdf manual. It does work for some of my data, but it doesn't for others.


I receive the following error message in R-Studio:

3: stats::optim(par = par, fn = fn, method = method, lower = lower, 
       upper = upper, control = control, ...)
2: Optimizer(par = pars, fn = fn, method = optimizer, lower = lower, 
       upper = upper, period = period, control = control)
1: ctmm.fit(track_h, GUESS)

regards
stefan


PS: 
here is the dataset I used: link
this is the code I used:
 

tracks <- as.telemetry('animalTracks.csv',timeformat="",timezone="UTC",projection=NULL,timeout=Inf,na.rm="row",drop=TRUE)

trackIDs <- names(tracks)
no_tracks <- length(trackIDs)

for(i in 1:no_tracks ){ #no_tracks) {
  track_i <- tracks[i]
  names(track_i) <- "1"
  track_h <- track_i$'1'
  GUESS <- ctmm.guess(track_h,interactive=FALSE)
  print(i)
  FIT <- ctmm.fit(track_h,GUESS)
  UD <- akde(track_h,FIT)

  assign(paste("UD", i, sep = ""), UD) 

}

messages.author: 40fd627580dd34f5
messages.subject: Re: R ctmm errors
parts:
Hi Stefan,

This CSV is interpreted as belonging to one individual because there is no MoveBank-style identity column. I do not know if that is intended or not, but as.telemetry() produces some warnings related to that.
Therefore, when you start indexing the telemetry object tracks, I do not think you are feeding a proper telemetry object into the later functions but probably just some columns of the telemetry object.

Best,
Chris
